Needs changes before merge.

This is a safety-tier review. I reviewed the full diff, including the UI changes from stack parent #3157.
The local trial merge with `upstream/main` succeeded at `03e05a64991301417bfd17c766fa512c1440950a`.
I used that main revision's `AGENTS.md` for the checks.

The reservation checks cover allocation, imports, edits, verification, and posting.
The standalone CLI checks the input before it writes output.
All 31 reservation pins passed.

### Local build and tests

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 155 steps in 5.9 minutes.
The gate built the selected test targets with `--no-run` before it ran them.

| Crate | Suite steps | Passed tests | Failed tests | Ignored tests |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| post | 33 | 321 | 0 | 0 |
| app | 101 | 1103 | 0 | 0 |
| UI | 18 | 1554 | 0 | 9 |

The UI library result was 1415 passed, zero failed, and seven ignored.
Pixel snapshot tests were not run.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
`cargo xtask gate light` passed all three steps in 2.6 minutes. Both light tests passed.
No GitHub runner was used.

### Extra suites run

These suites ran explicitly after the quick gate:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test continuous_4axis_part`: 10 passed.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests -p test_first_continuous_4axis_part.py`: 14 passed.

The diff changes no importer or STEP fixture. The extra kernel import suites do not apply.

### Independent mutations

I ran two mutations locally. Each failed at runtime. Each passed after I restored the guard.

| Mutation | Pin | Disabled guard | Restored guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Remove the reservation assignment in the machine parser | `reserved_tools_survive_stored_machine_round_trip` | RED: assertion at `crates/post/tests/tool_reservations.rs:55` | GREEN |
| Bypass the standalone reservation check | `standalone_post_refuses_cutter_in_reserved_probe_pocket_before_writing` | RED: assertion at `crates/post/tests/tool_reservations_cli.rs:41` | GREEN |

No mutation remains in the tree.

### Goldens

I checked the saved-project fixture change line by line.
`examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` adds only the T99 probe reservation.
Its exact project comparison passed. The trial-merged diff changes no NC or CL golden.

### Requested before merge

1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/browser_pane.rs:160`: Add before/after screenshots to this PR body. The diff includes the operator-side switch and viewport marker. This body has no screenshots. Parent #3157 has screenshots that can be linked here. Keep the images on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.
2. `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs:130`: Run the reached heavy lanes on the final head and record their results in the PR body. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` selects the app heavy lanes: 203 steps, including the release build. The body states that heavy lanes were not run. Current upstream `AGENTS.md`, “Heavy lanes at review,” requires these results before the PR is ready. Run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`. The full heavy lanes were not run in this review; the green light lane does not replace them.

The PR is mergeable, but these two readiness requirements remain open. Keep it as a draft.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Second safety read (Opus, read-only): clean

Scope: commit `757c65cf4` (the #2604 change). The PR is stacked on #3157. The other files in the diff are from #3157. I did not build. I read the diff and the changed files at the head.

**Wrong-output defects:** none found.

**Refusal law**
- `crates/app/src/tool_reservations.rs` `on_machine` refuses a non-probe tool at a reserved number or name. The message names the tool, the `T` number, the use (`probe` / `tool_setter`) and the machine model.
- No path renumbers an existing tool. `allocate` only picks numbers for new tools. It skips reserved numbers for a cutter. A probe takes a free reserved probe pocket, or it is refused.
- `program_refusal` runs at the start of `clash_per_machine`. `op_streams_by` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` calls it. Thus each app post (GUI, MCP, CLI, script) and the verification report refuse an unsafe assignment. A refused tool never posts.
- The standalone `post` binary runs `reservations::check_stream` before it opens the output. A refusal keeps an old output file (pinned by `standalone_post_keeps_existing_output_when_probe_pocket_is_used_for_cutting`).

**Entry points.** Each one checks when the command is created:
- `AddTool::new` (also `with_holder`, the MCP `add_tool` and the electrode command).
- `ChangeTool::new` (also the MCP `tool_edit`).
- `SetToolNumber::new` (also the MCP `tool_number_tools`).
- `ImportTools::with_options` (also the GUI library import and the script `import_tools`). It checks explicit numbers, kept numbers and new numbers.
Undo and redo keep the number that the command recorded.

**Machine files.** 18 Tormach files get `"reserved": [{ "number": 99, "use": "probe" }]`:
1100m-plus, 1100m, 1100mx, 1500mx, 24r, 770m-plus, 770m, 770mx-microarc4, 770mx-ml, 770mx, pcnc1100-s1, pcnc1100-s2, pcnc1100-s3, pcnc440, pcnc770-s3, pcnc770, xstech-pro, xstech.
No file loses a field or a legal tool number. `number_of_tools` is a count, not a number limit, so T99 does not conflict with it. No shipped example, golden or catalog entry uses T99. The two Tormach examples use T1 and T2 for cutters. No shipped example now refuses.

**Post side.** No `.nc` or `.cl` golden changes. One saved-project fixture changes: `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` adds the stored T99 reservation only. A legal program keeps its `T` words. Only a new probe on a Tormach machine now gets T99 instead of the next free number.

**Old projects.** A project that has a cutter on a reserved number opens without a crash. No number changes. Verification and post then refuse the tool by name (pinned by `existing_cutting_tool_in_probe_pocket_blocks_*` and `existing_cutting_tool_with_reserved_name_blocks_*`).

**Panics.** The new non-test code has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`.

**Pinning tests.** Each pin asserts a refusal or a number that did not exist before this change. Without the fix, `added_cutter_skips_probe_pocket_and_probe_takes_it` gets T1, and each refusal test gets `Ok`. Thus the pins fail without the fix. The author's mutation table agrees.

**Notes (not blockers, recommended follow-ups at P7):**
1. Merge order: #3157 is open. If this PR merges first, it also merges the #3157 `feat`. Merge #3157 first, as the body says.
2. A project stores its own copy of the machine. An old project on a Tormach machine has no `reserved_tools` in that copy. It gets no T99 protection until the user mounts the machine again. `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj` is such a project. Its output does not change. This is the old behaviour, not a regression.
3. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings.rs:276` compares with `tool_numbers::next_free`, which does not know reservations. On a machine that reserves the next free number, the editor can show a number that `AddTool` does not assign. A typed reserved number is still refused by `SetToolNumber`. The display can mislead, but the output is safe.

Not exercised: no build or test run by this read; the author's quick and heavy gates are on this head.

Coordinator, for @mkinney: #3284 carries the commits of #3157 (4484d6ed1 and the merge 4e93e1831), which has a change request and is a draft. Merge #3157 first, or retarget this PR to the #3157 branch.

- The base of this PR is `main`. A merge now brings the operator-side feature of #3157 to `main` without its review. Its files are in `crates/post/src/machine/` (`operator_side.rs`, `def.rs`, `mod.rs`, `parse.rs`), `crates/ui/src/` (`operator_side.rs`, `work_envelope.rs`, `interact.rs`, `state.rs`, `browser_pane.rs`), their tests, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` and `docs/decisions/2632-operator-side.md`.
- The second safety read (comment 7074965482) covers only the #2604 commit 757c65cf4. It is clean for that commit.
- I added `needs-rework` beside your `merge-ready`. I removed no label. The two collaborators decide on this PR.

The maintainer said in chat on 2026-11-22: "PR's with merge-ready cannot have needs-rework at the same time.."

This PR had both labels. The second safety read at head `757c65cf4` (NeoTech, 05:49:07Z) is clean. The PR is stacked on #3157, and #3157 is an open draft with `needs-rework`. This PR carries the commits of #3157, so it cannot merge before its parent. I removed `merge-ready`. The label `needs-rework` stays, because the stack parent blocks the merge. The clean review at head `757c65cf4` stands. The label `merge-ready` can return when #3157 is merged and this PR is refreshed on main.
